en.title: Maximum Rating Sum Without Skipping Two Movies in a Row
en.description: Traverse the movie rating array in its original order and choose a subsequence that maximizes the sum of the chosen ratings. You may not skip two or more movies in a row; skipping a single movie at the start and at the end is allowed. There is no extra requirement to choose at least one movie: when n=1 you may skip the only movie, and an empty selection has a rating sum of 0; when n≥2 you cannot skip all of them.
en.input: The first line contains n, and the second line contains n integers ratings[i]. Full original ranges: 1≤n≤100000, −1000≤ratings[i]≤1000.
en.output: Output the maximum rating sum that satisfies the constraint, as an exact integer, with no modulo.
en.explanation: Original example 1 chooses [2,4,−2] for 4. Original example 2 chooses [9,−1,4,5] for 17, and the original output is kept; the original explanation omitted −1 and wrongly claimed 9+4+5=17 while skipping two movies in a row, which this site explicitly corrects. The original [-1,−3,−2] allows choosing only the second item, which shows that a single skip at the start and at the end is valid; the original has no non-empty requirement, and the third public example, a single −1000→0, is added by this site.
hints: Consider two states separately: the last movie is chosen or skipped.
When the current movie is skipped, the previous one must be chosen.
Do not force both the first and the last movie to be chosen, and do not skip an all-negative array entirely.
